The image is a microscopic view (scale bar = 50 µm) showing:
- A central dark brown/amber conidial mass
- Multiple elongated, finger-like conidiophores radiating outward
- Oval to elliptical conidia at the tips of the conidiophores
- Light brown-gray coloration of the spores on brownish stalks

This morphology is characteristic of *Botrytis cinerea*, the causal agent of Gray Mold. Key matching features:
- Branched conidiophores with oval conidia at tips is hallmark Botrytis morphology
- The gray-brown spore mass on stalks matches the KB description: "spores are light brown-gray on black stalks"
- The scale (50 µm) is consistent with Botrytis conidiophore dimensions
- No chain-forming conidia (rules out Alternaria), no filiform conidia (rules out Septoria), no sporangia (rules out Rhizopus)
